The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity in many countries, including the United States. Consistent with macro-finance research on liquidity traps and credit channels, the FOMC cut the federal funds rate to the effective lower bound (0–0.25%) and initiated large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, alongside expanded repo operations, discount window support, and dollar swap lines, to stabilize market functioning and lower funding premia. Evidence from the credit channel and financial accelerator literature (e.g., Gertler–Gilchrist; Kashyap–Lamont–Stein) indicates such actions can compress external finance premia and support investment and employment, while inflation-forecast targeting insights (Svensson; Svensson–Woodford) underscore the benefit of keeping expectations anchored near 2% amid muted near-term inflation pressures. Overall, the near-term outlook remains weak but is partially buffered by these policy measures.
